name: dev.uptimepage/uptimepage
title: Uptimepage
description: Monitor uptime and incidents, run checks, and publish status updates from your Uptimepage org.

tools.name: acknowledge_incident
tools.description: Acknowledge an incident: take ownership and halt escalation. Internal/operational only — does NOT post anything to the public status page. Use post_incident_update for customer-facing updates. Asks for confirmation where the client can show a prompt; otherwise runs on the token's scope. Not read-only.

note.description:
Optional internal note recorded on the incident's activity timeline.
This is operator-facing, not published to the public status page.

tools.name: add_status_page_components
tools.description: Add monitors to a status page as public components, in one confirmation where the client can show a prompt. Give each a public_name the page's readers will understand, since the monitor's own name is operator-facing, and a public_group to file related components together. Monitors already on the page are reported as such rather than duplicated. detail_link_enabled publishes a per-monitor detail view that shows the monitor's real name and address, not public_name. groups adds monitor groups as live sections: a heading with the members' combined state, every member as its own row, and members that join or leave the group joining or leaving the page; members past the plan's public component limit stay off. Not read-only.

NewComponentArg.description: One monitor to curate onto a page.

detail_link_enabled.description:
Publish a per-monitor detail view. That view renders the monitor's
operator-side name and address, not `public_name`.

public_group.description:
Grouping label, at most 50 characters. Components sharing a label are
rendered together.

public_name.description:
Public-facing name, at most 80 characters. Defaults to the monitor's
own name, which is operator-facing and may not read well in public.

sort_order.description: Position on the page, ascending. Defaults to the order given.

NewSectionArg.description: One monitor group to show on a page.

heading.description: Public heading, at most 50 characters. Defaults to the group's name.

components.description: The monitors to add, in the order they should appear.

groups.description:
Monitor groups to show as live sections, by id from
`list_monitor_groups`. Every member gets a row, and members that join
or leave the group later join or leave the page.

tools.name: cancel_maintenance
tools.description: Cancel a maintenance window that has not ended. It leaves the status pages, stops holding paging, and stays listed under past as a record; subscribers already told about it are not sent a cancellation. To stop a running window early and keep it as completed work, use update_maintenance with end_now instead. Asks for confirmation where the client can show a prompt; otherwise runs on the token's scope. Not read-only.

inputSchema.description: Argument of the maintenance tools that take only an id.
inputSchema.title: MaintenanceIdArg

tools.name: create_maintenance
tools.description: Schedule a maintenance window for planned work on some monitors. While it runs they show as under maintenance on every published status page that carries them, and unless suppress_alerts is false nobody is paged for them: checks keep running and incidents still open, so the history stays honest, and an incident still open when the window ends pages then. Prefer this over pause_monitor for planned work. Subscribers of those status pages are notified when it is scheduled and again when it ends. Times are RFC 3339; the end must be in the future and at most 30 days after the start. Shows the window, its monitors, whether paging is held and where it is announced, where the client can show a prompt; otherwise runs on the token's scope. Not read-only.

ends_at.description: RFC 3339 end: in the future, after the start, and at most 30 days after it.

monitor_ids.description: The monitors the work touches, by id from `list_monitors`. At least one.

starts_at.description: RFC 3339 start. A start already past opens the window at once.

suppress_alerts.description: Hold paging for these monitors while the window runs. Defaults to true.

title.description: Shown on the status page and in subscriber notices. At most 200 characters.

tools.name: create_monitor
tools.description: Create a monitor for an http, tcp, ping, dns, tls_cert, domain_expiry, heartbeat or manual check. A manual monitor has nothing to probe; set its state afterwards with set_monitor_state. The check is run once before anything is saved and the result is shown to the user along with every setting it would apply; where the client can show a prompt, nothing is created unless they approve; otherwise the monitor is created on the token's scope and the trial result comes back with it. Bind it to alerts as you create it: pass channel_ids from list_notification_channels (this needs the channels:read scope), and if the org has no channel yet, say so rather than leaving a monitor that pages nobody. Leave regions unset unless the user named where they want the check to run from — omitted, it probes from the operator's default set, which is already the intended coverage; naming more regions than the plan allows is refused outright. Request headers and a request body can be set, but a credential must be referenced rather than pasted: write `Bearer {{ my_key }}` and call list_variables for the keys this org has. A URL carrying a username or password is refused, and browser flows cannot be created here — add those in the app. Not read-only.

NewCheck.description:
What a new monitor should check. Narrower than what the product supports on
purpose: no request headers, body or credentials, since those are literal
secrets an operator types once and this tool would carry through a chat log;
and no browser flow, which needs the fill values withheld everywhere else.
Add those in the Uptimepage app after the monitor exists.

body.description:
Request body, sent as given. `{{ key }}` references are resolved at
probe time, so a body may carry a secret by reference.

expected_body_contains.description: Text the response body must contain for the check to pass.

expected_status.description:
A single code like `200`, a range like `200-299`, or a list like
`200,201,204`. Defaults to `200-299`.

follow_redirects.description: Defaults to true, following at most 5 hops.

headers.description:
Request headers. A header that carries a credential
(`authorization`, `x-api-key`, `api-key`, `cookie`,
`proxy-authorization`) must reference an org variable rather than
spell the secret out: `Bearer {{ my_key }}`. Use `list_variables`
to find the key, and never paste the credential itself — this tool
refuses it, and a pasted one would live on in the chat log.

timeout_ms.description:
Defaults to 10000. A redirect counts as a pass only with
`follow_redirects`.

verify_tls.description:
Defaults to true. False accepts an invalid certificate, which a
`tls_cert` monitor is the better way to watch.

ip_version.description:
`any` (default) dials whichever of IPv6 and IPv4 connects first,
so a broken AAAA record or IPv6 firewall stays hidden. `ipv4` or
`ipv6` checks only that family and fails when the host has no
address in it. To watch both, create one monitor per family.

oneOf.description: A DNS record resolving, optionally to an expected value.

domain.description: Name to resolve. A `ptr` lookup also takes an IP address.

expected_records.description:
Every record the answer must hold and nothing else, written as a
result's `answers` shows them (`10 mail.example.com.` for MX, or a
bare `mail.example.com` to allow any preference). Any record
added, removed or changed fails the check. Not combined with
`expected_contains`.

resolver.description: Resolver to ask. Defaults to the agent's own.

critical_days.description: Days of remaining validity that fail it. Default 7.

warn_days.description: Days of remaining validity that degrade the check. Default 30.

oneOf.description:
An inbound ping from a job that is expected to report in. Nothing is
probed; the monitor fails when the ping does not arrive. The ping URL
and its token are shown in the app, never here.

grace_secs.description: Lateness tolerated before the monitor fails.

max_runtime_secs.description: Fail a run that starts and does not finish within this.

period_secs.description: How often the job is expected to report.

oneOf.description:
A service no probe can judge, such as a SIP trunk or a partner's back
office. Nothing is checked: it starts up, and `set_monitor_state` moves
it, opening and closing incidents like any other monitor.

RegionPolicyArg.description:
How many regions must agree a monitor is down before an incident opens.
`get_monitor` reads this back in the same shape, so the enum of legal modes
is one definition rather than a written-out list that can drift.

count.description:
Required with `mode: "count"`, ignored otherwise. Must be between 1 and
the number of regions the fleet has; `list_regions` reports them.

RegionPolicyMode.description: How the quorum is expressed. `count` carries its number in `count`.

alert_confirmations.description:
Consecutive failing checks before the monitor alerts. Minimum 1,
defaults to 2.

channel_ids.description:
Channel ids from `list_notification_channels` to alert. Omitting them
creates a monitor that pages nobody, which is worth saying out loud
rather than leaving for an outage to reveal. The channels themselves are
set up in the app, since they hold the tokens and addresses.

interval_secs.description:
Seconds between checks, held to the plan's floor and the check kind's
own floor. Omit it to get the cadence the app's own picker opens this
kind at, which is well above the hard minimum for the slow-moving kinds:
a certificate is checked twice a day, a domain registration daily.

name.description: What the operator will see in lists and alerts.

notify_recovery.description: Whether recovery is announced. Defaults to true.

recovery_period_secs.description:
Seconds a recovered monitor must stay healthy before its incident
closes; a failure confirmed inside the window keeps the incident open,
so a flapping service reads as one outage. 0 to 1800; 0 closes on the
confirming checks alone. Defaults to 180 on an HTTP, TCP, ping, DNS or
flow monitor and 0 on the rest. Not for a manual monitor.

regions.description:
Probe regions to run the check from, as ids from `list_regions`. Omit
unless the user named the places they want covered: omitting takes the
regions `list_regions` flags `default_selected`, which is the coverage
the operator chose, capped at the plan's region cap and falling back to
the control plane's own region when nothing is flagged. A vantage point
can be offered without being on by default, so the full catalog is not
the thorough answer. Rejected for a heartbeat, which is pinged rather
than probed, and a set larger than a `max_regions` `list_regions`
reports is refused outright, not trimmed to fit.

tags.description: At most 50, each at most 50 characters.

tools.name: create_monitors
tools.description: Create several monitors at once, with one confirmation covering the batch where the client can show a prompt. Every check is run once first and all the results are shown together, so a misconfigured endpoint is visible before anything is saved. An item that fails validation or its trial run is reported in the results and the rest are still created. Prefer this over repeated create_monitor calls whenever the user names more than one thing to watch: it costs them one prompt instead of many. Same per-monitor fields and same limits as create_monitor. Not read-only.

alert_confirmations.description:
Consecutive failing checks before the monitor alerts. Minimum 1,
defaults to 2.

channel_ids.description:

creates a monitor that pages nobody, which is worth saying out loud

monitors.description:
The monitors to create. Each is validated and probed before the single
confirmation covering the batch.

tools.name: create_status_page
tools.description: Create a status page. It is created unpublished unless you pass enabled, so its components can be curated before anyone can read it. The slug is the page's public address: it is first-come across the platform and moving it later breaks every existing link, so confirm it with the user rather than inventing one. Pass access with protected true to make it private: only the listed domains and addresses can open it, after signing in with a code sent to their email (Team plan). Add monitors to it with add_status_page_components. Not read-only.

PageAccessArg.description:
Who may open a status page; the same shape as the REST `access` field. As a
write it replaces what is stored, whole.

protected.description:
Private when true: only people a way in lets through can open the
page: the addresses and domains in `rules`, by a code sent to their
email, or anyone with the page password. False makes it public again
and keeps the list and the password for next time.

rules.description:
Who can get an email code, up to 500 entries. Read back, these are
customer data.

session_days.description:
Keep a sign-in, by email or password, for 7, 30 or 90 days. Omit to
keep it until sign-out.

kind.description:
`domain` lets in every address at `value` (`example.com`); `address`
lets in one person (`name@example.com`).

PageEmailAccessArg.description: The emailed-code way in, and the passkeys that shortcut it.

enabled.description: Defaults to true. A private page needs it or the password.

passkeys_enabled.description: Let viewers save a passkey after an email sign-in. Defaults to true.

recheck_days.description:
Ask passkey viewers for an email code again after 30, 90 or 365 days.
Omit to never ask.

PagePasswordAccessArg.description:
The page password way in. The password itself never passes through here:
it is set in the app, the API or Terraform.

enabled.description:
Anyone with the page password can open the page. Turning it on needs
one already set; turning it off keeps it and signs out everyone who
came in with it.

access.description: Make it private from the start. Omit for a public page.

enabled.description:
Defaults to false: a page is created dark so components can be curated
before anyone can read it.

name.description: Page display name, at most 80 characters.

slug.description:
URL slug, lowercase. This is the page's public address and cannot be
guessed back later, so pick it deliberately.

tools.name: get_flow_runs
tools.description: A browser flow monitor's recent runs over a window (1h/24h/7d/30d): every declared step with its outcome and duration, the step a failure stopped on, and the page the browser saw. Use this to answer why a login check failed. Read-only.

id.description: The monitor id (from `list_monitors`), of a `flow` monitor.

tools.name: get_flow_step_trend
tools.description: How long each step of a browser flow monitor takes over a window (1h/24h/7d/30d), and how far it has moved: per step the earliest and latest mean duration, their ratio, and how many runs passed or failed it. Use this to spot a step drifting toward failure while the monitor still reports up. Read-only.

id.description: The monitor id (from `list_monitors`), of a `flow` monitor.

tools.name: get_incident
tools.description: One incident: affected monitor, what opened it, severity, open/resolved times, error sample, the full operator-update timeline, and the status pages an incident with no monitor is posted to. For an incident another tool's alert opened, also the source and what the tool sent: labels, annotations, links and the worst severity it reported. Read-only.

inputSchema.description: Argument of the incident tools that take only an id.
inputSchema.title: IncidentIdArg

tools.name: get_incident_metrics
tools.description: Incident metrics over a trailing window (default 30 days): MTTA/MTTR in seconds, total incidents, counts by severity and state, auto- vs human-resolved, and the noisiest monitors. Read-only.

window_days.description: Trailing window in days (1..=365). Defaults to 30 when omitted.

tools.name: get_maintenance
tools.description: One maintenance window: title, description, start and end, phase, the monitors it covers, and whether it holds their paging. Read-only.

inputSchema.description: Argument of the maintenance tools that take only an id.
inputSchema.title: MaintenanceIdArg

tools.name: get_monitor
tools.description: One monitor's full configuration — everything the check asserts (expected status, body match, headers, timeout, redirect and TLS policy), the regions it probes from, and how it alerts (failing checks before it pages, whether recovery is announced, the reminder interval, the multi-region quorum, and the ids of the channels it notifies) — with its current state, last error, and 24h/30d uptime. Every field update_monitor can change is readable here, in the shape that tool takes. Read this before judging whether a response should have passed, or before changing a monitor. Credentials are withheld. Read-only.

tools.name: get_monitor_history
tools.description: One monitor's history over a window (1h/24h/7d/30d): uptime, latency series, a per-region split of the same window, failures with error text, and incident windows. Pass `region` to narrow it to one probe region and tell a partial outage from a total one. Read-only.

region.description:
Narrow uptime, the latency series, and the region breakdown to one probe
region (an id the monitor is assigned to, from `get_monitor.regions`).
Omit for every region together.

tools.name: get_org_health
tools.description: Org health summary: per-state monitor totals and the worst currently-failing monitors. The one-shot answer to 'what is broken right now?'. Read-only.

tools.name: get_org_usage
tools.description: Which org this connector is bound to, and the account's resource usage against plan limits: monitors, status pages, members, components, channels, alert sources, and key policy values. Caps are pooled across every org the account owns, so the counts can exceed what this one org holds. Read-only.

tools.name: get_status_page
tools.description: One status page: name, public URL, enabled, subscriber email time zone, its components with each linked monitor's current state, and the monitor groups it shows as sections with their members. Read-only.

tools.name: list_alert_sources
tools.description: The org's alert sources: tools such as Prometheus Alertmanager, Grafana and Datadog, or a script, that send their alerts here so they open incidents and page through the org's rotations. Per source: id, operator-set name, kind (alertmanager, grafana, datadog, generic), whether it is enabled (paused when not) or held by the plan, routes_to_nobody when its policy, the org default and its channels all reach no one, its escalation policy and channels, and when its last event arrived. The ingest URL and token are withheld: sources are set up in the Uptimepage app. Read-only.

tools.name: list_incidents
tools.description: List the org's incidents: incident id, affected monitor, what opened it (origin, with the alert source for an incident another tool's alert opened), severity, open/resolved times, and latest update phase. Defaults to currently-open ones; pass state="all" with an optional from/to window (default: last 30 days) for resolved history, and monitor_id to narrow to one monitor. Read-only.

cursor.description:
Opaque pagination cursor from a previous call's `next_cursor`. It
carries the whole query, so send it on its own: any other filter passed
alongside it is ignored rather than silently changing the page.

from.description:
RFC 3339 start of the window. Defaults to 30 days ago. An incident that
is still running is listed however long ago it opened.

state.description:
Which incidents to return: `open` (default) for the ones still running,
or `all` to include resolved ones inside the window.

to.description:
RFC 3339 end of the window. Defaults to now. Incidents that opened after
it are excluded, running or not.

tools.name: list_maintenance
tools.description: List maintenance windows: title, start and end, phase (upcoming, active, completed or cancelled), the monitors each covers, and whether it holds their paging. status narrows to active, upcoming or past (ended or cancelled); the default is all, latest start first. Cursor-paginated. Read-only.

oneOf.description: Ended or cancelled, most recent first.
Every window, cancelled ones included, latest start first.

cursor.description:
Opaque pagination cursor from a previous call's `next_cursor`. It
carries the whole query, so send it on its own.

tools.name: list_monitor_groups
tools.description: The org's monitor groups, empty ones included: name, whether the group alerts as one (a member's failure opens one group incident that pages the group's channels, and the members' own stay quiet), member count, the group incident open now, its channels, reminder interval, whether another member going down sends a message, and tags. Read-only.

tools.name: list_monitors
tools.description: List monitors with optional state/type/tag filters and cursor pagination. Each item carries its current state and last-checked time. Read-only.

inputSchema.description: `list_monitors` arguments. All filters are optional; omit for everything.

cursor.description: Opaque pagination cursor from a previous call's `next_cursor`.

tag.description: Filter to monitors carrying this exact tag.

inputSchema.title: ListMonitorsArgs

tools.name: list_notification_channels
tools.description: The org's notification channels: id, operator-set name, kind (email, slack, telegram, webhook, and so on), and whether the channel is enabled. Two flags say a channel is not working even where it reads as ready: awaiting_verification for an email address nobody confirmed, and not_delivering for an enabled channel whose recent alerts all failed to arrive. auto_bind_tags is the channel's tag rule: it also pages any monitor carrying one of those tags, so a monitor with no binding can still be covered. Channel settings are withheld, since they hold webhook URLs and bot tokens. Channels are created in the Uptimepage app, not here. Read-only.

tools.name: list_regions
tools.description: The fleet's probe regions: id, display name, city, country, continent, and whether each is on by default for a new monitor. Reports `max_regions` only when the plan reaches fewer regions than the catalog lists, so a set too large to be accepted is visible before it is sent. Use it to pass a valid `region` to get_monitor_history, and to read where a check would run from. This is a catalog, not a menu to fill: leave `create_monitor.regions` unset unless the user named the places they want covered. Read-only.

tools.name: list_status_page_viewers
tools.description: List who signed in to a private status page: each viewer's address, first and last visit, saved passkeys, whether they subscribe by email, and whether they are blocked; and for the page password, which names nobody, the devices signed in with it, its last sign-in and the wrong tries in 24 hours. Addresses are customer data. Read-only.

tools.name: list_status_pages
tools.description: List the org's status pages: slug, name, public URL, enabled. Cursor-paginated. Read-only.

cursor.description: Opaque pagination cursor from a previous call's `next_cursor`.

tools.name: list_tags
tools.description: Every tag in use across the org's monitors, most-used first, with how many monitors carry each. Pass one back as the `tag` filter to list_monitors. Read-only.

tools.name: list_variables
tools.description: The org's reusable variables: key, and whether it is a secret. Values are never returned, and a secret's value is never even read. Write a variable into a monitor's header or body as `{{ key }}`, which is resolved when the check runs: this is how an authenticated check is built here, since pasting the credential itself is refused. Variables are created and edited in the app, not here. Read-only.

tools.name: pause_monitor
tools.description: Pause a monitor (stop its checks until resumed). For planned work, create_maintenance holds paging instead while the checks keep running. Asks for confirmation where the client can show a prompt; otherwise runs on the token's scope. Not read-only; idempotent.

tools.name: post_incident_update
tools.description: Post a public, customer-facing update to an incident's status-page timeline (phase + message). This is what your subscribers and status-page visitors see. Asks for confirmation where the client can show a prompt; otherwise runs on the token's scope. Not read-only.

inputSchema.description:
`post_incident_update` argument: appends a public, customer-facing entry to
the incident's status-page timeline.
inputSchema.title: PostIncidentUpdateArgs

tools.name: post_maintenance_update
tools.description: Post an update to a maintenance window: say the work is running late, that it finished, or what changed. Works on an upcoming, running or completed window (a completed window is read-only otherwise, so this is how to add a closing note), not on a cancelled one. The update shows on the status pages that show the window and goes to their email and webhook subscribers; it cannot be edited or removed. Asks for confirmation where the client can show a prompt; otherwise runs on the token's scope. Not read-only.

message.description:
What readers should know now, up to 2000 characters: the work runs
late, it finished, or what changed. Write it for the people reading
the status page, and give any time with its zone.
Markdown: `**bold**`, `_italic_`, `[links](url)`, lists and `` `code` ``;
every line break is kept and raw HTML shows as typed.

tools.name: publish_incident
tools.description: Publish an incident so it appears on every status page carrying the affected monitor, optionally seeding the public title and description. An incident with no monitor needs `status_page_ids` naming the pages to show it on; the list replaces its pages, so start from `get_incident`'s `status_page_ids`. Status-page subscribers may be notified. Asks for confirmation where the client can show a prompt; otherwise runs on the token's scope. Not read-only; idempotent.

inputSchema.description:
`publish_incident` argument. The optional narration seeds what customers
read on the status page; omitted fields keep whatever is stored.

public_description.description: Public summary shown under the headline.

public_title.description: Public headline shown on the status page.

status_page_ids.description:
Status page ids (from `list_status_pages`) for an incident with no
monitor; replaces its pages, so start from `get_incident`'s
`status_page_ids` to add or drop one. Leave unset for a monitor's incident,
which shows on the pages carrying that monitor.

inputSchema.title: PublishIncidentArgs

tools.name: resolve_incident
tools.description: Resolve an incident (mark the operational state resolved). Internal only — does not post to the public status page. Asks for confirmation where the client can show a prompt; otherwise runs on the token's scope. Not read-only.

note.description:
Optional internal note recorded on the incident's activity timeline.
This is operator-facing, not published to the public status page.

tools.name: resume_monitor
tools.description: Resume a paused monitor (restart its checks). Asks for confirmation where the client can show a prompt; otherwise runs on the token's scope. Not read-only; idempotent.

tools.name: run_check_now
tools.description: Run a check on a monitor immediately and record the result. Asks for confirmation where the client can show a prompt; otherwise runs on the token's scope. A down result may fire the org's normal alerts. Heartbeat monitors cannot be probed (they wait for your systems to ping them). Not read-only.

tools.name: set_monitor_state
tools.description: Set the state of a manual monitor: up, degraded or down. A manual monitor has no probe; its state is whatever an operator last set, for a service only people can judge, such as a SIP trunk, a carrier link or a partner's back office. Down or degraded opens an incident within about 30 seconds, which pages the monitor's channels unless a maintenance window holds it, and shows on its status pages as a major outage or degraded performance; up closes the incident. A paused monitor, or one the plan no longer covers, keeps the state and acts on it once it runs again. The note becomes the incident's cause, so make it a reason a responder can act on. Refused for any other kind of monitor. Asks for confirmation where the client can show a prompt; otherwise runs on the token's scope. Not read-only; idempotent.

ManualStateArg.description: What an operator says about a manual monitor.

oneOf.description: Working, but impaired. Shows as degraded performance on status pages.
Not working. Shows as a major outage on status pages.

note.description:
Why, in one line of at most 200 characters. It becomes the incident's
cause and reaches whoever is paged. Omit for none; it replaces the
previous note.

tools.name: unpublish_incident
tools.description: Hide a published incident from the public status pages again. Its operator timeline is untouched. Asks for confirmation where the client can show a prompt; otherwise runs on the token's scope. Not read-only; idempotent.

inputSchema.description: Argument of the incident tools that take only an id.
inputSchema.title: IncidentIdArg

tools.name: update_maintenance
tools.description: Edit an upcoming or running maintenance window: its title, description, start, end, the monitors it covers (monitor_ids replaces the whole set) or whether it holds their paging. end_now ends a running window at once and keeps it as completed work. A completed or cancelled window is history and is refused. Shows the old and new value of every field before it runs, where the client can show a prompt; otherwise runs on the token's scope. Not read-only.

inputSchema.description:
`update_maintenance` arguments. Every field except `id` is optional; omit
what should stay as it is.

end_now.description: End a running window now. Cannot be combined with `starts_at` or `ends_at`.

ends_at.description: RFC 3339, in the future. To stop a running window now, send `end_now` instead.

monitor_ids.description:
Replaces the whole set, by id from `list_monitors`. Read the window
first: a monitor left out stops being covered.

suppress_alerts.description: Hold paging for its monitors while it runs.

inputSchema.title: UpdateMaintenanceArgs

tools.name: update_monitor
tools.description: Change how loudly a monitor is watched: check interval, alert confirmations, recovery notices, reminder interval, tags, group, the multi-region detection quorum, and which notification channels it alerts (channel_ids replaces the whole set, and needs the channels:read scope). It cannot change what the check watches — name, address, assertions, expected status, headers, body, probe regions and owner are refused. A monitor managed by Terraform is refused outright. Shows the old and new value of every field before it runs, where the client can show a prompt; otherwise runs on the token's scope. Not read-only.

RegionPolicyArg.description:
How many regions must agree a monitor is down before an incident opens.
`get_monitor` reads this back in the same shape, so the enum of legal modes
is one definition rather than a written-out list that can drift.

count.description:
Required with `mode: "count"`, ignored otherwise. Must be between 1 and
the number of regions the fleet has; `list_regions` reports them.

RegionPolicyMode.description: How the quorum is expressed. `count` carries its number in `count`.

inputSchema.description:
`update_monitor` arguments. Every field except `id` is optional; omit what
should stay as it is. Name, address or URL, assertions, expected status,
headers, body, probe regions and owner are not editable here, and passing
one is an error rather than a silent no-op.

alert_confirmations.description:
Consecutive failing checks before the monitor alerts. Minimum 1. Raising
it quietens a flapping monitor at the cost of alerting later.

channel_ids.description:
Replaces the whole set of alerted channels, by id from
`list_notification_channels`. Read the monitor first: a channel left out
of this list stops being alerted. An empty list silences the monitor.

group_name.description: Operator-side grouping label. Send `null` to clear it; omit to keep it.

interval_secs.description:
Seconds between checks. Held to the plan's floor and the check kind's
own floor, whichever is higher.

notify_recovery.description: Whether recovery is announced to the monitor's channels.

recovery_period_secs.description:
Seconds a recovered monitor must stay healthy before its incident
closes, 0 to 1800. Raising it folds a flapping monitor's short outages
into one incident, at the cost of announcing recovery later.

tags.description:
Replaces the whole tag list. Read the monitor first: a tag left out of
this list is removed. At most 50 tags, each at most 50 characters.

inputSchema.title: UpdateMonitorArgs

tools.name: update_monitor_group
tools.description: Change a monitor group: its name, whether it alerts as one (a member's failure opens one group incident that pages the group's channels, and the members' own stay quiet), which notification channels the group incident alerts (channel_ids replaces the whole set, and needs the channels:read scope), the reminder interval, and whether another member going down sends a message. Turning alert as one on or off changes only failures that start afterwards. A group managed by Terraform is refused outright. Shows the old and new value of every field before it runs, where the client can show a prompt; otherwise runs on the token's scope. Not read-only.

inputSchema.description:
`update_monitor_group` arguments. Every field except `id` is optional; omit
what should stay as it is.

alert_again.description:
Whether another member going down sends a message or only a timeline
line.

alert_as_one.description:
Turns alerting as one on or off. Only failures that start afterwards
follow the new setting; an incident open now ends the way it started.

channel_ids.description:
Replaces the whole set of channels the group incident alerts, by id
from `list_notification_channels`. Read the group first.

name.description: New name, at most 50 characters. Members keep their group.

renotify_interval_secs.description:
Seconds before the first reminder while the group incident stays
unacknowledged; 0 turns reminders off, otherwise at least 60.

inputSchema.title: UpdateMonitorGroupArgs

tools.name: update_status_page
tools.description: Rename a status page, move it to a new slug, publish and unpublish it, change who may open it, or set the IANA time zone of its subscriber emails. An omitted field is left alone. Changing the slug moves the public URL and breaks existing links. access replaces the page's access settings and list whole: protected true makes it private to the listed domains and addresses (Team plan), and removes subscribers the list does not cover; protected false makes it public again and keeps the list. Not read-only; idempotent.

PageAccessArg.description:
Who may open a status page; the same shape as the REST `access` field. As a
write it replaces what is stored, whole.

protected.description:
Private when true: only people a way in lets through can open the
page: the addresses and domains in `rules`, by a code sent to their
email, or anyone with the page password. False makes it public again
and keeps the list and the password for next time.

rules.description:
Who can get an email code, up to 500 entries. Read back, these are
customer data.

session_days.description:
Keep a sign-in, by email or password, for 7, 30 or 90 days. Omit to
keep it until sign-out.

kind.description:
`domain` lets in every address at `value` (`example.com`); `address`
lets in one person (`name@example.com`).

PageEmailAccessArg.description: The emailed-code way in, and the passkeys that shortcut it.

enabled.description: Defaults to true. A private page needs it or the password.

passkeys_enabled.description: Let viewers save a passkey after an email sign-in. Defaults to true.

recheck_days.description:
Ask passkey viewers for an email code again after 30, 90 or 365 days.
Omit to never ask.

PagePasswordAccessArg.description:
The page password way in. The password itself never passes through here:
it is set in the app, the API or Terraform.

enabled.description:
Anyone with the page password can open the page. Turning it on needs
one already set; turning it off keeps it and signs out everyone who
came in with it.

inputSchema.description:
`update_status_page` argument. Every field but `slug` is optional; an
omitted field is left as it is.

access.description:
Replace who may open it: make it private, change its list, or make it
public again.

new_slug.description: New slug. Changing it moves the public URL and breaks existing links.

slug.description: The page to change, by its current slug.

timezone.description:
IANA time zone for the times in its subscriber emails, such as
`Europe/Berlin`. The page itself shows each visitor their own time.

inputSchema.title: UpdateStatusPageArgs

tools.name: update_status_page_component
tools.description: Change how one monitor is presented on a status page: its public name, description, group or position; or, with section_id, a group section's heading. An omitted field is left alone. A section member's heading is its section's, so its public_group does nothing. Not read-only; idempotent.

inputSchema.description: `update_status_page_component` argument. An omitted field is left as it is.

heading.description:
The section's public heading, at most 50 characters; blank shows the
group's name.

monitor_id.description:
The monitor id whose curation is being changed. Send this or
`section_id`.

public_group.description: Ignored on a section member, whose heading is the section's.

section_id.description: A section (from `get_status_page`) whose `heading` is being changed.

inputSchema.title: UpdateComponentArgs
